topics.topic: AuditEntry identity and continuity across restored store histories
questions: Is an AuditEntry identified only by its sequence number within the currently stored history, or must each store history have an identity that also scopes the entry?

When the original and restored histories mint different AuditEntries with the same sequence number, what is an AuditEntry's identity across histories, and does a store history itself have an identity recorded by Registry?

When the restored history reuses sequence numbers that the lost history had already used after the backup, is an AuditEntry identified only within one store history, and if so what identifies or scopes that history?

If an audit entry was present in the backup and erased later in the lost history, does restoration make that same AuditEntry present again, create a restored copy with a new identity, or treat the new history as a branch in which that entry was never erased?

judgement.why: Registry exposes only the current store history; lost-history entries cannot be read or acted on, and immutable backup entries have identical observable facts whether treated as the same entities or restored copies.

topics.topic: MigrationClosure ownership and at-most-one scope across restored histories
questions: Is MigrationClosure cardinality scoped to each store history, so the same production instance may acquire a new closure after restoring a pre-import backup, or is the restored store considered a new instance for this model?
Does MigrationClosure belong to the Registry instance or to one store history, and can the same continuing instance create a second closure after restoring a pre-import backup?
Is MigrationClosure a fact of the Registry instance, of its current store, or of one store history, and within which scope is there at most one?

quotes:
A store lost before a checked backup holds the import
loses the import with it, and the import may then be made again.

None; absent, then present for the rest of the store's history. A store
restored after a loss from a backup made before the import begins a history
without it (R0-89).
judgement.why: The closure is scoped to the current store history: restoration from a pre-import backup removes it and permits the continuing production installation to import again.

questions: Does “the backup's last number” mean the highest sequence number ever allocated in the state captured by the backup, or merely the greatest number among audit entries still retained in that backup; and what value applies when it contains no entries?
